admissionOpaque.$comment: C# BridgeProtocol and Host validate/serialize paths enforce UTF-16 string bounds and the UTF-8 serialized frame byte limit; JSON Schema length counts Unicode code points.

oneOf.$comment: Unicode NFC and UTF-16 label bounds are runtime-only invariants enforced by C# BridgeProtocol and Host validate/serialize paths.

executionBinding.$comment: Parent-grant equality of programId, nodeId and nodeAttempt is a runtime-only invariant enforced by C# BridgeProtocol and Host validate/serialize paths.

reachable.description: Whether the actor can act on this target from where it stands. null means undecided (nobody measured it), never false.

accessible.description: Whether this exit's target location passes the engine's own accessibility gate (Game1.isLocationAccessible). Omitted by the Mod, never null, when the leg was not measured; absent must never be read as false.

kind.description: One of the closed vocabulary of location-fixed interaction points. The four `mine_*` words name the Buildings-layer tile indices `MineShaft.checkAction` dispatches on (MineShaft.cs:3057-3096); the other two name the engine's own tile properties.

actionWord.description: The engine's own first word at this tile (`MinecartTransport` out of `Action: MinecartTransport Default`), or null where the engine carries no word - a mine ladder is a tile index and has nothing to quote.

family.description: The WIRE FIELD NAME of the discovery family this row explains, from the closed set of families that report exclusions (`ExclusionReportingCapabilities` in farmhandexecutioncontroller.cs). One array still attributes every row to the list whose emptiness it explains, and a row cannot name a list nobody publishes. `tools/check-stardew-discovery-exclusions.mjs` compares this enum with the Mod's declaration by name.

reason.description: One of the closed vocabulary of reasons a family withheld subjects it could see. A reason is admitted only when the engine itself refuses the same action on the same subject today; a filter the engine does not share is a defect in discovery, not a reason.

count.description: How many subjects this family's filter took for this reason. A COUNT, never an identity: the subject the filter removed is by definition not addressable. At least one, because a zero-count exclusion is not an exclusion. No upper bound: `harvestWhereabouts` and `wateringWhereabouts` count a whole crop population across every loaded location, which is thousands on a large farm.

hoeDirt.description: `GameLocation.GetHoeDirtAtTile(tile) is not null` read when the row was published: whether a HoeDirt already occupies this tile, which is the state the row reports. `true` is a tile the actor has already hoed - the `plant_seed`/`fertilize_tile`/`water_crop` target and the record of work already done - and `till_soil` refuses it with `soil_already_tilled`; `false` is ground the Hoe still admits. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

upgradeLevel.description: The upgrade tier of a tool that upgrades. ABSENT for a tool that cannot be upgraded: the engine gives those -1 (MilkPail, Shears) and a level is a tier, not a sentinel. Absent means "this tool does not upgrade", never "unknown".

isForage.description: `Object.isForage()` for this object, read when the row was published. It is the one predicate that separates this family from `itemTargets`, and `pickup_forage` refuses a target whose answer has since turned false. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

watered.description: `HoeDirt.isWatered()` for this tile, read when the row was published. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it. Added 2026-11-05 because `water_crop` decides from it and the row carried no such fact.

harvestable.description: `HoeDirt.readyForHarvest()` for this tile, read when the row was published. Optional at the wire for the same reason as `watered`.

daysToHarvest.description: The sum of `CropData.DaysInPhase`, the same derivation the `Crops` data answer publishes. Absent together with the other `Data/Crops` fields when `cropFactsUnknown` names why.

regrowDays.description: `CropData.RegrowDays` as the engine reports it: -1 means the crop does not regrow (the common case), 0 means it regrows the day it is picked.

harvestMethod.description: The engine's harvest-method word (`grab`/`scythe`), the same spelling `harvestTargets` publishes.

isRaised.description: `CropData.IsRaised`: a trellis crop, planted on a tile that stops being walkable. Added 2026-11-09 with the rest of the `Data/Crops` half: the fact was already askable through `look_up({table:"Crops"})` and was never asked.

seasons.description: `CropData.Seasons`, as the engine's own season keys (`Utility.getSeasonKey`): spring, summer, fall, winter.

fullyGrown.description: `Crop.fullyGrown`: this plant finished its phases. Deliberately NOT the same question as `harvestable` (`HoeDirt.readyForHarvest()`): a crop just picked and regrowing is fully grown and not yet harvestable.

tileBlockedNow.description: Whether a farmer cannot walk onto this tile at the moment of publication - `GameLocation.isCollidingPosition` over the tile's own 62x62 box, the admission test `PathFindController.cs:222` makes. Not `GameLocation.isTilePassable`, which reads only the map's Back and Buildings layers and reports a trellis crop as open ground. A reading of one instant, tied to the snapshot's `revision`.

cropFactsUnknown.description: Why the `Data/Crops` fields above are absent, as one token (`crop_facts_unknown:crop_data_missing`). The only value today is `crop_data_missing`: the engine resolved no data row for this crop, so there is no such fact rather than a default one. A silence here would let a reader plan on an invented `isRaised: false`.

readyForHarvest.description: `HoeDirt.readyForHarvest()` for this tile, read when the row was published. `harvest_crop` refuses an unready crop, so the row states the fact rather than leaving it to be inferred from the discovery filter. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

forageCrop.description: `Crop.forageCrop` for this crop, read when the row was published. `harvest_crop` refuses a forage crop (the forage path is `pickup_forage`), and `scythe_crop` publishes such a tile only once it is dead. Optional at the wire for the same reason as `readyForHarvest`.

harvestMethod.description: `Crop.GetHarvestMethod()`, the engine's own `HarvestMethod` member lower-cased, read when the row was published. It is the fact the crop actions branch on rather than the engine call name: `HoeDirt.performUseAction` harvests a `grab` crop through `Crop.harvest` and hands a `scythe` crop to the scythe branch (HoeDirt.cs:488-529), so `harvest_crop` admits only `grab` and `scythe_crop` only `scythe`. The target version's enum declares exactly these two members.

canPlantThisSeedHere.description: `HoeDirt.canPlantThisSeedHere(seed.ItemId, isFertilizer: false)` for this tile and this seed, read when the row was published: the engine's own season and raised-crop admission, which refuses an out-of-season seed, a location whose season rule rejects it, and a raised crop whose footprint covers the actor. `plant_seed` refuses a tile whose answer has since turned false. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

crop.description: `HoeDirt.crop is not null` for this tile, read when the row was published: whether a crop already occupies it, which is the other fact `plant_seed` refuses on. False on every row discovery publishes. Optional at the wire for the same reason as `canPlantThisSeedHere`.

canApplyFertilizer.description: `HoeDirt.CanApplyFertilizer(fertilizer.QualifiedItemId)` for this tile and this fertilizer, read when the row was published: the engine's own admission (a tile that already carries fertilizer, a potted tile, or a mismatched fertilizer refuse here). `fertilize_tile` refuses a tile whose answer has since turned false. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

machineData.description: `Object.GetMachineData() is not null` read when the row was published: whether the object carries its own `Data/Machines` rows, which is what makes it a machine `machine_inspect`/`machine_load`/`machine_collect_output` can address rather than an ordinary placed object. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

harvestWhereabouts.description: One loaded map's ready-for-harvest crop count. The nearest tile is published ONLY for the map the actor stands on: a coordinate on another map is not an address, so a row for any other map carries its count and neither coordinate. The pair is both-or-neither.

currentToolSlot.description: The farmer's active tool slot (Farmer.CurrentToolIndex), or null when no tool is held. The tool-family actions take a slot that must equal this index, so it cannot be judged statically.

currentToolSlotItem.description: The qualified item id occupying `currentToolSlot`, whatever its kind, or null when the slot is empty. Published because the held-slot actions (dress_mannequin, set_sign_display, deposit_silo_hay, ...) demand that the named slot hold the exact item AND be the held one, so the slot index alone does not say what the companion is holding.

chestsSummary.description: The current location's chests in one row: how many, how many items they hold, and how many are at the engine's own chest capacity. Location-wide rather than radius-bounded, and with no location member of its own - it describes `location`.

pendingLevelUps.description: The engine's pending level-ups as `skill@level` (0 Farming ... 5 Luck), what the next night boundary will ask the companion to decide. Bounded at 8, published 2026-10-19 so the harness stops learning the pair by parsing a refusal.

pendingLevelUpChoices.description: The pending profession MILESTONES (levels 5 and 10), each with both candidates the engine's own rule offers, the engine's own titles and descriptions, and the level-5 constraint a level-10 pair depends on. Published so the companion can SEE the choice before `respond_level_up` writes one.

professions.description: The actor's own profession ids, the set a `respond_level_up` milestone branch writes and a fresh read confirms.

levelUpChoice.description: One pending profession milestone: the `(skill, level)` pair, the two candidate ids in the game's own card order (branch_a = left, branch_b = right) with the engine's own title and description, and the level-5 profession a level-10 pair continues from (omitted when the pair does not depend on an earlier choice).

isWeeds.description: `Object.IsWeeds()` for this object, read when the row was published: the litter predicate that decides whether a scythe can cut it (category -999 with "weeds" in the name), and the fact `cut_weeds` re-checks on the target. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

readyForHarvest.description: `HoeDirt.readyForHarvest()` for this tile, read when the row was published. The scythe harvest branch fires only on it (HoeDirt.cs:711-731); the dead branch ignores it. Optional at the wire so a Mod older than this field still validates; current Mods always publish it.

dead.description: `Crop.dead` for this crop, read when the row was published. It is the discriminator between the generation's two terminals: a dead tile can only be CLEARED and drops nothing (`HoeDirt.cs:732-735`, `Crop.harvest` refuses it), whatever its harvest method or readiness. Optional at the wire for the same reason as `readyForHarvest`.

forageCrop.description: `Crop.forageCrop` for this crop, read when the row was published. The harvest branch refuses a forage crop; such a tile is published only once it is dead. Optional at the wire for the same reason as `readyForHarvest`.

chestsSummary.description: The current location's chests as one bounded line: how many there are, how many items they hold between them, and how many have no free slot left. `fullCount` counts containers at the engine's own `Chest.GetActualCapacity()`, where `Chest.addItem` stops accepting a new stack.

nativeNotices.$comment: Raw native HUD notice text observed in the action's synchronous window. Bounded transport shape only; Host forwards it verbatim and never interprets a notice.

kind.description: What the live thing IS for this lane, in the Mod's own words. `placed_furniture` is a piece in `location.furniture` - the room's own bed, sofa or rug - which `place_owned_object` can add to but no object kind can describe, because furniture never sits in `location.objects`. `empty_pedestal` is a pedestal in `location.objects` that holds nothing, which is the only state `place_item_on_pedestal` can address.

rotation.description: The piece's live `Furniture.currentRotation`: one quarter-turn of its own cycle. `null` for every kind that is not a piece of furniture - never 0 or -1, because 0 is a legal rotation and a sentinel that reads as a value gets compared as one.

rotations.description: The size of the piece's own rotation cycle, from Data/Furniture (`Furniture.rotations`). Below 2 the engine's `rotate()` is a no-op, which is why `rotate_furniture` refuses such a piece by name instead of turning nothing. `null` for every kind that is not furniture.

seedSupplyTarget.description: One plantable seed the actor HOLDS: the count she holds, and - when a shop stocks it - what the menu charges, whether that shop's own hours query says it is open, and WHERE that shop is. The address half is EXACTLY ONE of `shopDestination` (the counter is in the location the actor stands in: the very `shopTargets` row `shop_purchase` resolves), `shopLocation` (the room the counter is in when it is elsewhere) and `shopLocationUnknown` (why neither could be read). A price and an open-now answer with none of the three would read as a shop she can walk to.

shopDestination.description: Where a shop's counter IS, in the terms a walk can start from: the room, the exact `shop_purchase` target id in it, the tile that target stands on, and the name to show while walking. Every member is taken from the `shopTargets` row the Mod already publishes - never a second identity minted for this family - so this destination and the row `shop_purchase` resolves are one fact.

wateringWhereaboutsRow.description: One loaded map's dry-crop count. The nearest tile is published ONLY for the map the actor stands on: a coordinate on another map is not an address, so a row for any other map carries its count and neither coordinate. The pair is both-or-neither.
